answer: A seat is one permitted diversion point on a canal, filed under a state water-right number, with a sealed flowmeter by the vine rows. Every fifteen minutes the meter signs an interval total; the seed names an hour, and the seat posts that slice plus a photo of the gauge seal. Diversions sharing a headgate, ditch company or permit holder fold into one vote and forfeit 80,000 POA each. Each headgate costs $2,400 installed and $600 a year to report, so a thousand seats sink $3 million into concrete. A ditch rider walks the ridge at dusk with a lantern and counts gates, not straws in them.
